text:
Maria Chen: Quick share — ran the 'prefetch-pulse' KV-cache experiment across us-east (H100) and eu-west (A10). Goal: reduce p99 tail due to sloshy sequence-length waves without blowing up memory. Summary below + config + short notes. https://redwood.internal/bench/2169123456

Ajay Patel: Nice. What mixes/seqlens did you use?

Maria Chen: seqlen mix = [32:40%, 128:40%, 512:20%], injected wave pattern every 30s to mimic bursty chat traffic. Prefetch pulse params: window=8, depth=4, cooldown=12s. Eviction: segmented-LRU (hot/cold), fallback to ttl after 600s.

Samir Lopez: Can you drop the raw numbers? hitrate vs latency across regions?

Maria Chen: Sure — pasted small table (p50/p95/p99 in ms, hitrate %). H100 (us-east): throughput 1.8k tok/s per GPU

```
H100 (us-east)   | hit%  | p50  | p95  | p99
----------------------------------------
baseline (no-pref) | 62%  | 12ms | 48ms | 210ms
prefetch-pulse      | 76%  | 14ms | 39ms | 120ms
```
A10 (eu-west): throughput 950 tok/s per GPU

```
A10 (eu-west)     | hit%  | p50  | p95  | p99
----------------------------------------
baseline (no-pref) | 58%  | 18ms | 65ms | 320ms
prefetch-pulse      | 71%  | 21ms | 52ms | 180ms
```
Notes: prefetch-pulse increased hit% by ~12-14 points and cut p99 roughly ~40-50% relative to baseline, but p50 went up slightly due to prefetch overhead.

Devon Kim: Interesting. Did you see memory pressure on A10 with depth=4?

Maria Chen: Yes — A10 reached ~78% VRAM under peak with segmented-LRU; H100 stayed ~62%. If we bump depth to 6 on A10, VRAM > 90% and we see OOM risk under sustained 512 spikes.

Lia O'Connor: What about kernel choices? Were you using the new batchable-kernel-2 or the old path?

Maria Chen: Ran both. batchable-kernel-2 reduced p95 by ~6% on A10 for the prefetched cases but increased page-evict churn by ~8% (more small memcpy ops). On H100 the kernel diff was negligible.

Samir Lopez: Any per-seqlen hit curves? I'd expect 32-token requests to have higher hit% and lower latency obviously.

Maria Chen: Yup. Quick breakdown (prefetch-pulse on H100): 32 -> hit 88% (p99 45ms), 128 -> hit 74% (p99 110ms), 512 -> hit 54% (p99 220ms). The pulse helps the 128 bucket most.

Ajay Patel: Did you try dynamic windowing based on recent seqlen histogram? Adaptive windows could avoid prefetching for long-run 512 storms.

Maria Chen: Ran one pilot: dynamic-window = min(12, 2 * median_seqlen_bucket). That cut unnecessary prefetch by ~22% and improved p50 back to baseline while keeping p99 ~10% worse than fixed-pulse (so tradeoff).

Devon Kim: From infra POV, what's the capacity-sizing recommendation? More GPUs or tune prefetch?

Maria Chen: Short answer: for mixed traffic with waves, tune prefetch-pulse window to 6-8 on H100, 4-6 on A10 and keep segmented-LRU thresholds tighter (hot threshold lower). If you need strict p99 SLA, add ~20% GPU buffer in eu-west A10 clusters for safety; H100 needs ~10% headroom.

infra-bot: Artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-bench/2169123456/prefetch-pulse-report.tar.gz (contains traces, flamegraphs, csvs).

Lia O'Connor: Can we run a 48h canary in eu-west with dynamic-window toggled on and eviction=segmented? I want to see multi-day slosh effects.

Maria Chen: Yes — scheduling now. Experiment config: `--prefetch-mode pulse --window 6 --depth 4 --dynamic-window true --evict segmented --evict-ttl 600`

Ajay Patel: I'll update the runbook and add a short checklist for when to prefer prefetch-pulse vs conservative mode.

Samir Lopez: Action items: Maria -> roll canary (eu-west, A10) 48h; Devon -> monitor VRAM alarms + kernel churn; Lia -> add grafana panels for seqlen-hist and prefetch-savings.

Maria Chen: Thanks everyone — will post follow-up after 24h and attach the canary dashboards. :rocket:
